How This Document Is Meant to Be Used

Purpose & Intended Audience

This is a working reference for City of Toronto Council members, City staff across departments (Shelter, Support and Housing Administration; City Planning; Toronto Public Health; Toronto Paramedic Services), partner agency leadership, and — deliberately — the students, teachers, and community members whose engagement makes any of this durable. It is not a finished policy platform. It is a bank of vetted starting points, organized so that a committee, a working group, or a single staff person under deadline pressure can find something genuinely useful in minutes rather than days.

How Solutions Are Organized & Rated

Every solution carries five plain-language ratings: Difficulty (political and operational complexity, 1–3), Timeline (realistic implementation window), Cost (relative order of magnitude, 1–3), and Evidence Strength (1–3, how well-supported the approach is in research or comparable-city practice). None of these ratings are precise forecasts — they are calibrated judgment calls meant to help you triage, not a substitute for your own due diligence, costing, and legal review.

New: Step-by-Step Guides & Profession-Tailored Notes on Every Solution

Every one of the 1,001 solutions now expands to include a six-step implementation guide (mandate → bottleneck → pilot → funding path → frontline test → review point) written specifically against that solution's own named partners, bottleneck, timeline, and cost tier — and four profession-tailored action notes drawn from real job titles relevant to that solution's domain, each tagged with one of eight broad lenses (frontline, clinical, policy, operations, legal, finance, community, technical). Use the "View guidance through the lens of" selector above the Solutions Bank to highlight the notes most relevant to your own role across the entire bank at once.

New: Professional Pathways — Where to Start by Role

Beyond the per-solution notes, the new Professional Pathways section (below) is a set of twelve hand-written onboarding guides — for frontline case managers, shelter operators, urban planners, elected officials, clinicians, community organizers, legal advocates, data professionals, educators, emergency responders, Indigenous-serving organizations, and employment professionals — each walking through a specific, ordered sequence of solutions from this bank that are most relevant to that role, with the reasoning for the order included, not just a list.

Glossary of Terms Used in This Bank

Every acronym below appears somewhere in the 1,001 solutions or the guidance around them. Defined once here rather than repeated inline throughout, so the solution cards themselves stay readable.

What This Document Is Not

This is not legal, financial, clinical, or engineering advice. It is not a substitute for consultation with people who have lived experience of homelessness, whose participation should shape any of these solutions before adoption — not after. It does not encode any hidden agenda, dark pattern, or persuasion technique; every interactive feature here exists solely to help you find, compare, and act on the information faster.

Hand-Written · Role-Specific Onboarding

Professional Pathways: Where to Start by Role

Twelve genuinely written guides — not generated summaries — each walking through a specific, reasoned sequence of solutions for one professional role. Every reference below links directly to the matching card in the Solutions Bank. Find your role, or the one closest to it, and start there.

The Solutions Bank

Your search, filters, and reviewed/favourited items are saved locally to your device only — never transmitted anywhere.

Decision-Support Scaffolding

Meta-Prompt Chains for Bottlenecks, Gates & Locks

These are structured sequences of prompts and steps designed to help a working group — with or without an AI assistant — work through the specific procedural, legal, and political bottlenecks that recur across this solutions bank. Every chain ends with a mandatory human accountability checkpoint. None of these chains are designed to bypass legal, ethical, privacy, or safety review — they are designed to get a stuck conversation to the point where the right accountable person can make a real decision, faster.

Separate Reference Library

Tools & Information to Deepen Understanding

Distinct from the solutions bank above: this is a curated library of data sources, evidence bases, legal resources, funding programs, training providers, and international case studies referenced throughout this document. These are informational pointers, not procurement endorsements — always verify current terms, licensing, and suitability before use.

Required Disclosure

Attributions & Licensing

Design & Engineering Patterns

This document's interaction patterns (collapsible sections, sticky table of contents, client-side search, offline-first storage architecture) draw on widely published, openly documented patterns from the accessible web-design and progressive-web-app communities. No proprietary or license-restricted code was copied from any GitHub repository or elsewhere; patterns were adapted and re-implemented from first principles in vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript specifically for this document, with no external runtime dependencies.

Typography

This document requests the Fraunces and Libre Franklin typefaces (both open-source, SIL Open Font License) where available on the reader's system or via a locally cached copy, and falls back gracefully to system serif and sans-serif faces when unavailable — consistent with the no-external-font-loading requirement for full offline reliability.

Research & Evidence Sources

Evidence claims throughout this bank draw on publicly available research from the Canadian Observatory on Homelessness, the Mental Health Commission of Canada's At Home/Chez Soi study, CMHC, the Canadian Alliance to End Homelessness, and comparable-city case studies (Helsinki, Vienna, Medicine Hat, Houston, and others) as referenced inline. This is a synthesis and translation document, not a peer-reviewed publication — always verify current figures against primary sources before citing them externally.

License

This document and its underlying content are offered for the City of Toronto's use and adaptation in service of addressing homelessness. Reuse, adapt, and redistribute freely in service of this goal; attribution to this document as a source is appreciated but not required.

Zero-Harm & Anti-Inversion Notice

This tool was built to help systems serve people experiencing homelessness better — never to identify, surveil, profile, penalize, or coerce any individual. It stores no data outside your own device, sends nothing to any server, and includes no hidden telemetry. If any feature in this document could plausibly be inverted to target or harm the people it is meant to serve, please treat that as a defect and remove it. All analytics on this page (the progress HUD) are optional, entirely local, fully transparent in their source code above, and resettable at any time via the button in the HUD panel.
